title: Atom vs. Molecule

references.label: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class 11 — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

summary: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains that element's chemical identity. A molecule is two or more atoms chemically bonded together — either of the same element or different elements.
explanation: Atoms are the fundamental building blocks; they can exist independently for noble gases, but most elements are more commonly found combined into molecules. A molecule can be formed from atoms of a single element (like O₂ or O₃, both forms of oxygen) or from atoms of different elements (like H₂O), in which case it's also specifically called a compound.

comparison.left: Atom: smallest unit of an element
comparison.right: Molecule: two or more bonded atoms

comparison.left: Always a single element by definition

comparison.right: Common — most matter exists as molecules

genZNote: Same atoms, different relationship status — a lone atom is single, a molecule is atoms that decided to bond (sometimes with their own kind, sometimes not).
